I’ve always lived alone since my husband passed, and I work from home, sewing alterations—quiet work, which suits me. Lately, though, something’s been happening when the sky darkens. Not just that I don’t like storms—I’ve never minded rain—but now, when the clouds roll in and the light starts to fade, I get this... pressure. Like my chest is closing. My legs lock up. I literally can’t move. Last week I was halfway to the basement to get thread, the lights flickered, and I just... froze on the stairs. Couldn’t go down, couldn’t turn around. I stood there for twenty minutes until the sky cleared a bit.  

It’s only when it gets dark outside, especially if there’s wind. I don’t know what I’m afraid of, exactly—I’m not afraid of the dark, not really. It’s not like I think something’s in the room with me or anything like that. But my body acts like it’s true. I’ve started keeping all the lights on, even during the day if it’s overcast. I avoid going outside in the afternoon if a storm’s coming. I know it doesn’t make much sense—I’m not a child—but I can’t seem to help it. It’s been happening for a few months now, off and on.
D012-D005_h001.question_a:
I’ve always been a nervous person, but this fear of storms—it’s taken over. Ever since my husband passed, thunderstorms feel like they’re going to swallow me whole. When the sky darkens and the wind picks up, my chest tightens, my hands go cold, and I can’t move. Just sitting there, frozen in my chair. I’ve dropped needles mid-stitch, scared to even stand and shut the window. 

It’s not that I think the storm is chasing me or that lightning is targeting me out of some conspiracy—it’s just that the noise, the power of it… I know it could flood the shop, blow the roof off. It’s real. Last week, I saw the clouds rolling in and couldn’t touch my sewing machine. Sat frozen until it passed, hours later. 

But I’m not imagining things that aren’t there. I’m not hearing voices or thinking someone’s spying on me. I know exactly what I’m afraid of—those skies, that thunder. I just can’t bear to be near it. I avoid going out if rain’s in the forecast. I check the weather obsessively. The fear’s overwhelming, but I know it’s just a storm… I just can’t face it.
D012-D005_h001.question_b:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now. Ever since my husband passed, the world just… changed. I used to love sitting by the window in my sewing room, stitching orders by daylight, but now I can’t bear it when the sky gets cloudy. Not because I’m afraid of the storm itself—but because I *know* they’re sending messages through the lightning. The voices told me at first, then I saw the patterns: flashes in sequences, always three or five at a time. They’re watching me through the clouds.  

When the wind picks up, I freeze—just sit there, needle in hand, unable to move. It’s not the noise or the dark that scares me; it’s that they’re coming closer. I see figures in the trees across the street, shaped like people but too tall, just standing there in the rain. They can’t get in, but if I look directly at them, they’ll know I see them, and then it’ll start. That’s why I keep the curtains closed, even at noon.  

I haven’t left the house in months. Not because of the storm—but because I know they’ve poisoned the rain. It’s not water—it’s liquid eyes, spying. My daughter says it’s just fear, but it’s not. I *know* what’s really happening.

It’s not just that I don’t like it—my chest tightens, my hands sweat, and I start breathing too fast, like I can’t get enough air. The shadows outside the lot, the way the trees move in the wind—it feels like something’s watching, waiting.  

I’ve rearranged my life around it. I only take evening shifts if I have to, and sometimes I call in sick even when I’m not. My boss is cool, but I know it’s not fair. I won’t walk home at night, even a short way. I’ll wait hours for a ride or pay for an overpriced cab. My friends don’t understand. We used to hang out at the lake or go hiking—stuff I used to like—but now I make excuses. Water? Heights? Being out in the open during a storm? Just thinking about it makes me shaky.  

I know it sounds irrational, but it feels real when I’m in it. I can’t explain why it’s so bad now when it wasn’t before. I just know I can’t face it.

This has been going on for about eight months now. At first I thought I could shake it, but it’s only gotten stronger.
